title: Red Dead Redemption 2
provenance: played here on the Steam copy, M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r6, 2026-09-11
notes: Plays on engine x64-crossover26.3-r6 or later. The game uses its own Vulkan renderer (through MoltenVK), so the graphics mode setting does not apply to it; keep DXMT for the Rockstar launcher, which needs it. What r6 changes: MoltenVK refused the linear-tiled 3D, mipmapped and array images the game creates (Metal cannot back those with linear memory) and RDR2 exited at 98 per cent of its first load on every earlier engine; Highball's MoltenVK now creates such images with optimal tiling instead, and the game loads in about a minute, reaches its main menu and plays. Tested at 1280x720 windowed (Settings/system.xml under Documents/Rockstar Games/Red Dead Redemption 2, <screenWidth>, <screenHeight>, <windowed value="1" />); fullscreen at the display's resolution is untested and Highball does not yet honour fullscreen mode requests (highball#72). About 34 fps in the prologue snow with the game's Safe preset. Keyboard note: the first key after the window regains focus is ignored by the game, press it again. History, for anyone chasing the other renderer: DirectX 12 through D3DMetal initialises and then faults inside D3DMetal about 30 seconds in (execute fault at 0x20019008070c10 after 'Not implemented'), and <API>kSettingAPI_DX11</API> from some guides does nothing because RDR2 has no Direct3D 11 renderer (it falls back to Vulkan). CodeWeavers' MoltenVK 1.2.10 fork reaches 84 per cent then hits the game's own out-of-memory dialog (1729 host-coherent refusals). All of that is closed by the r6 MoltenVK. Honest playability note (2026-09-12, M1 Pro): the ride reads 40 fps on the Metal HUD but the GPU line sits near 49 ms a frame and the image judders; it runs, it is not comfortable to play here. The Rockstar Social Club overlay (SocialClubHelper.exe, GPU and renderer processes) used about three quarters of a core beside the game. A newer chip has a different GPU budget; reports wanted. Lead, not verified (2026-09-12): in Settings/system.xml, vSync 0 and fsr2Index 2 (FSR 2 balanced) cut the GPU time in the opening cutscenes from about 49 ms to 14 ms and freed the counter from its 39.9 pin; the ride was not re-measured because that run ended in a winevulkan assert (vkGetPipelineCacheData thunk, exit code 3, once in 14 runs here). The Rockstar Social Club overlay's helper processes used about 45 percent of a core beside the game.

knownIssues.symptom: On engines before r6: loads to about 98 per cent, opens a window and exits without a frame (Vulkan), or crashes about 30 seconds in with DirectX 12 selected in system.xml.
knownIssues.cause: MoltenVK 1.4.1 refuses linear-tiled 3D, mipmapped and array images (fixed in r6's MoltenVK). D3DMetal answers a D3D12 call the game needs with 'Not implemented' (not fixable here).
knownIssues.fix: use engine x64-crossover26.3-r6 or later and leave the game on its default Vulkan renderer.

knownIssues.symptom: One vertex shader fails to compile to Metal (gl_CullDistance emitted into an undeclared struct member) and the driver logs many bytes_per_row assertions during loading.
knownIssues.cause: SPIRV-Cross's Metal output for cull distance, a known limitation (SPIRV-Cross issue 1403, MoltenVK issue 1484: Metal has no cull distance built-in and the translator emits an array member the output struct lacks), and the row pitch of the game's linear 2D textures.
knownIssues.fix: none needed so far: nothing visibly missing in the prologue. Recorded so a texture glitch later has a lead.

verified.fps: about 40 by the counter on the prologue blizzard ride at 1280x720 windowed, but uneven: GPU near 49 ms a frame on the ride, visibly juddery, not what the maintainer would call playable on an M1 Pro (third run 2026-09-12, 0.9.7, engine r7); 55-60 in the menus and the intro montage, 35 in the opening cutscene
verified.how: Steam, Rockstar launcher signs in, first-run prompts (brightness, subtitles, audio), main menu, Story: intro montage, opening cutscene, then the blizzard ride under keyboard control (W moves the horse). Zero faults in two runs of 15 and 12 minutes.
